main_text.p: hibet Plutarchus, civitatis jure excide-runt. A quo tempore non alii quàm tali matrimonio editi, jurantibus parentibus aut propinquis, in tabulas iftas recipiebantur. Tabulæ hæ curialium communes quoque sunt dictæ: in quas qui referebantur, & ante & poft Periclis legem, eorum nominibus parentum etiam nomina cum populo, ad quem pertinebant, adscribebantur. Totaque hæc actio δοκιμασία, & actionis præsides ac genitalium inspectores δοκιμαστῆς appellabantur. Rei huic destinatum fere fuit certum anni tempus, tertius scilicet dies festi, quod Apa-turia dicebant. Et quod dictum de filiis, quos parentes ex se genuerant, idem etiam valuisse videtur de iis, quos ritè adoptaverant, ut ex verbis Demosthenis in Boeorum colligi posse exiftimamus. Triennio post sequebatur professio altera, & probatio apud populares anno ætatis profitentium decimo octavo, ut eidem placet Sigonio verosimili ratione nixo: actum nomina eorundem refe-rebantur in album, quod ληξιαρχικὸν γραμματεῖον [?] vocabant. Ea enim inscriptione, ut omnis reliqui juris civium & civilium munerum, ita & adeundarum ac pro arbitrio administrandarum hae-
[?] Greek words in this paragraph are transcribed from the scan; the accents and letters of δοκιμασία, δοκιμαστής and ληξιαρχικὸν γραμματεῖον are uncertain and should be checked.

page.notes: The Greek words δοκιμασία and δοκιμαστής are printed in a worn state; their accents and some letters are doubtful, so they carry [?]. The Greek phrase at "rebantur in album" is printed with worn letters and is only approximately read. The first line of the page starts with a fragment of the previous paragraph, marked cont="true". The right margin shows only small stains and fragments of the neighbouring page (around "tem-", "turia", "nixo", "refe-" and "redi"); these are not printed notes and have not been transcribed. The printed catchword "redi" and the signature "G 2" are read from the foot of the page. No marginal notes are legible on this page.
